summary: Little Space Outpost is a browser-playable STEM game for children ages 7–12. Players join ASTRO and a three-astronaut crew to scout a lunar landing site, build a habitat, oxygen system, solar panels, radiation shelter, and greenhouse, then manage five simulated Moon days. Each day, they choose whether to grow food, save power, or charge the shelter while air and food are consumed. A randomly timed practice solar event makes planning ahead matter. The project turns lunar-outpost trade-offs into accessible choices and replayable outcomes. NASA/CCMC DONKI is credited as a space-weather reference; the prototype does not fetch live or archived DONKI data.
details:
Players progress through Explore, Build, and Survive. In Explore, they inspect candidate lunar sites. In Build, they place a habitat, oxygen system, solar panels, radiation shelter, and greenhouse on suitable spots; the greenhouse is gated until power and supplies are ready.

During the five-day mission, each day consumes one unit of air and food and adds one power. The player chooses to spend 2 power to grow 3 food, save 2 power while food is still consumed, or spend 2 power to add 2 shields. A randomly scheduled solar event on mission day 2–4 demonstrates why shelter planning matters; shields can reduce the game’s practice radiation dose.

The prototype is designed for ages 7–12, with plain-language guidance, touch-friendly controls, and replayable outcomes. It is an educational simplification, not an engineering or forecasting tool. It was built with Phaser 3, JavaScript, HTML, and CSS. Python with Pillow, NumPy, and SciPy was used for asset preparation, and Playwright for browser testing. Its goal is to make connected outpost needs tangible and spark STEM discussion.
dataRefs: NASA/CCMC DONKI — Space Weather Database Of Notifications, Knowledge, Information
